transcript.text: Good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining this medication-safety huddle. As you know, the hospital introduced the intravenous anticoagulant protocol on Monday, and it's currently stocked in the automated dispensing cabinets and ordered through the electronic medication record. Before I sign off on the afternoon decision to allow use of this protocol on the night shift, I need to hear operational findings from each department. We'll follow our standard checklist: I'll call on pharmacy, laboratory medicine, nursing education, and clinical information technology in turn. Each department will report its operational findings and any required safeguards. I'll record each requirement, and then I'll go back around to confirm each one is accurately captured before I sign the final decision. Let's begin with Pharmacy. What operational findings do you have regarding the IV anticoagulant protocol?

transcript.text: I confirmed that the anti-Xa analyzer is unavailable for calibration until Friday at 17:00. During that period, the laboratory's approved replacement is an aPTT test every six hours for patients receiving this protocol.
